-- Co-op with more than two players (added by the SR2 co-op mod, appended to ug_lib.lua).
-- Player names come from player_names_get_all(); the local player is LOCAL_PLAYER, every other name is a remote player.

COOP_FAR_DISTANCE = 1000000

-- The number of entries of list from index 1 up to the first nil. SR2 runs Lua 5.0 with the base library only,
-- so there is no getn; this is the one counter of the library.
function coop_count(list)
	local count = 0
	while list[count + 1] ~= nil do
		count = count + 1
	end
	return count
end

-- The names of the players other than the local one, in a table indexed from 1.
-- Without any other player the list holds REMOTE_PLAYER, so everything built on it behaves like the two-player script.
function coop_remote_players()
	local remotes = {}
	local count = 0
	for i, p in pairs(player_names_get_all()) do
		if type(p) == "string" and p ~= LOCAL_PLAYER then
			count = count + 1
			remotes[count] = p
		end
	end
	if count == 0 then
		remotes[1] = REMOTE_PLAYER
	end
	return remotes
end

-- True when name is the name of a remote player.
function coop_is_remote_player(name)
	if name == nil or name == LOCAL_PLAYER then
		return false
	end
	for i, p in pairs(coop_remote_players()) do
		if p == name then
			return true
		end
	end
	return false
end

-- True when inside[name] is true for every remote player (also when there is none).
function coop_all_remotes_in(inside)
	for i, p in pairs(coop_remote_players()) do
		if not inside[p] then
			return false
		end
	end
	return true
end

-- True when inside[name] is true for any remote player.
function coop_any_remote_in(inside)
	for i, p in pairs(coop_remote_players()) do
		if inside[p] then
			return true
		end
	end
	return false
end

-- The distance of the nearest remote player to object, measured with dist_fn(player, object).
function coop_nearest_remote_dist(dist_fn, object)
	local measure = coop_native(dist_fn)
	local nearest = COOP_FAR_DISTANCE
	for i, p in pairs(coop_remote_players()) do
		local current = measure(p, object)
		if current < nearest then
			nearest = current
		end
	end
	return nearest
end

-- True when any remote player is farther than distance from object.
function coop_any_remote_farther_than(dist_fn, object, distance)
	local measure = coop_native(dist_fn)
	for i, p in pairs(coop_remote_players()) do
		if measure(p, object) > distance then
			return true
		end
	end
	return false
end

-- Sets inside[name] to value (default true) for every remote player closer than distance to object;
-- true when there was any.
function coop_mark_remotes_near(inside, dist_fn, object, distance, value)
	local measure = coop_native(dist_fn)
	if value == nil then
		value = true
	end
	local any = false
	for i, p in pairs(coop_remote_players()) do
		if measure(p, object) < distance then
			inside[p] = value
			any = true
		end
	end
	return any
end

-- Kills every remote player that has inside[name] set.
function coop_kill_remotes_in(inside)
	for i, p in pairs(coop_remote_players()) do
		if inside[p] then
			COOP_NATIVE.character_kill( p )
			COOP_NATIVE.character_ragdoll( p, 100 )
		end
	end
end
-- Mission support for more than two players (added by the SR2 co-op mod, appended to ug_lib.lua after coop_helpers.lua).
-- The scripts keep per-player state in tables keyed by player name and ask "both players ..." or "either player ...".

-- A per-player default: a table is copied one level, any other value is used as it is.
function coop_copy_default(value)
	if type(value) ~= "table" then
		return value
	end
	local copy = {}
	for k, v in pairs(value) do
		copy[k] = v
	end
	return copy
end

-- A table keyed by player name: local_value for the local player, a copy of remote_value for every remote player.
-- A remote player that has no entry yet (it is in the game, but was not when the table was made) gets a copy on its first read.
function coop_player_table(local_value, remote_value)
	local state = {}
	state[LOCAL_PLAYER] = local_value
	for i, p in pairs(coop_remote_players()) do
		state[p] = coop_copy_default(remote_value)
	end
	setmetatable(state, {
		__index = function(table_, name)
			if coop_is_remote_player(name) then
				local value = coop_copy_default(remote_value)
				rawset(table_, name, value)
				return value
			end
			return nil
		end
	})
	return state
end

-- True when state[name] is true for the local player and for every remote player.
function coop_all_players_in(state)
	return state[LOCAL_PLAYER] and coop_all_remotes_in(state)
end

-- True when state[name] is true for the local player or for any remote player.
function coop_any_player_in(state)
	return state[LOCAL_PLAYER] or coop_any_remote_in(state)
end

-- Sets state[name] = value for every remote player.
function coop_set_remotes(state, value)
	for i, p in pairs(coop_remote_players()) do
		state[p] = value
	end
end

-- True when state[name] == value for every remote player.
function coop_all_remotes_equal(state, value)
	for i, p in pairs(coop_remote_players()) do
		if state[p] ~= value then
			return false
		end
	end
	return true
end

-- True when state[name] == value for any remote player.
function coop_any_remote_equal(state, value)
	for i, p in pairs(coop_remote_players()) do
		if state[p] == value then
			return true
		end
	end
	return false
end

-- The name of the remote player nearest to object (REMOTE_PLAYER when there is no other player).
function coop_nearest_remote(object)
	local nearest = nil
	local nearest_dist = nil
	for i, p in pairs(coop_remote_players()) do
		local dist = COOP_NATIVE.get_dist(p, object)
		if nearest == nil or dist < nearest_dist then
			nearest = p
			nearest_dist = dist
		end
	end
	return nearest
end

-- The calls below take the call as it is written in a two-player script, fn followed by its arguments with REMOTE_PLAYER
-- among them, and make it once per remote player with REMOTE_PLAYER replaced by that player.

-- fn(...) once per remote player.
function coop_each_remote(fn, ...)
	local at = coop_remote_arg_index(arg)
	for i, p in pairs(coop_remote_players()) do
		local copy = coop_args_for(arg, at, p)
		fn(unpack(copy, 1, copy.n))
	end
end

-- True when fn(...) is true for any remote player.
function coop_any_remote(fn, ...)
	return coop_first_remote(fn, unpack(arg)) ~= nil
end

-- True when fn(...) is true for every remote player.
function coop_all_remotes(fn, ...)
	local test = coop_native(fn)
	local at = coop_remote_arg_index(arg)
	for i, p in pairs(coop_remote_players()) do
		local copy = coop_args_for(arg, at, p)
		if not test(unpack(copy, 1, copy.n)) then
			return false
		end
	end
	return true
end

-- The first remote player for which fn(...) is true, or nil.
function coop_first_remote(fn, ...)
	local test = coop_native(fn)
	local at = coop_remote_arg_index(arg)
	for i, p in pairs(coop_remote_players()) do
		local copy = coop_args_for(arg, at, p)
		if test(unpack(copy, 1, copy.n)) then
			return p
		end
	end
	return nil
end

-- The first remote player with state[name] == value, or nil.
function coop_first_remote_equal(state, value)
	for i, p in pairs(coop_remote_players()) do
		if state[p] == value then
			return p
		end
	end
	return nil
end

-- Disables the controls of every remote player who is in a vehicle and stops that vehicle.
function coop_stop_remote_vehicles()
	for i, p in pairs(coop_remote_players()) do
		if COOP_NATIVE.character_is_in_vehicle(p) then
			COOP_NATIVE.player_controls_disable(p)
			COOP_NATIVE.vehicle_stop_do(p)
		end
	end
end

-- True when state[name][key] is true for any remote player (state holds one table per player).
function coop_any_remote_at(state, key)
	for i, p in pairs(coop_remote_players()) do
		if state[p][key] then
			return true
		end
	end
	return false
end

-- True when state[name][key] is greater than limit for any remote player.
function coop_any_remote_above(state, key, limit)
	for i, p in pairs(coop_remote_players()) do
		if state[p][key] > limit then
			return true
		end
	end
	return false
end

-- A random remote player.
function coop_random_remote()
	local remotes = coop_remote_players()
	return remotes[rand_int(1, coop_count(remotes))]
end

-- The names of all players: the local player, then every remote player.
function coop_all_players()
	local players = { LOCAL_PLAYER }
	for i, p in pairs(coop_remote_players()) do
		players[coop_count(players) + 1] = p
	end
	return players
end

-- The distance of the remote player farthest from object, measured with dist_fn(player, object).
function coop_farthest_remote_dist(dist_fn, object)
	local measure = coop_native(dist_fn)
	local farthest = 0
	for i, p in pairs(coop_remote_players()) do
		local current = measure(p, object)
		if current > farthest then
			farthest = current
		end
	end
	return farthest
end

-- A copy of the list of names with REMOTE_PLAYER replaced by every remote player.
function coop_expand_remote(names)
	local expanded = {}
	for i, name in ipairs(names) do
		if name == REMOTE_PLAYER then
			for k, p in ipairs(coop_remote_players()) do
				expanded[coop_count(expanded) + 1] = p
			end
		else
			expanded[coop_count(expanded) + 1] = name
		end
	end
	return expanded
end
-- A sync mask (SYNC_LOCAL 1, SYNC_REMOTE 2, SYNC_ALL 3) names the local player and the whole remote side. For
-- customization_item_wear and inv_weapon_enable_or_disable_all_slots the adapter also reads a player number above those
-- two bits and sends the remote part to that player only; the game's natives test only the two bits.
COOP_SYNC_TARGET_STEP = 16
COOP_PLAYER_NUMBER = {
	["#PLAYER2#"] = 2, ["#PLAYER3#"] = 3, ["#PLAYER4#"] = 4, ["#PLAYER5#"] = 5, ["#PLAYER6#"] = 6, ["#PLAYER7#"] = 7,
	["#PLAYER8#"] = 8, ["#PLAYER9#"] = 9, ["#PLAYER10#"] = 10, ["#PLAYER11#"] = 11, ["#PLAYER12#"] = 12,
}

-- sync_table[player], its remote part narrowed to that player while there is more than one remote player.
function coop_sync_for(sync_table, player)
	local sync = sync_table[player]
	local number = COOP_PLAYER_NUMBER[player]
	if number == nil or (sync ~= SYNC_REMOTE and sync ~= SYNC_ALL) or coop_count(coop_remote_players()) < 2 then
		return sync
	end
	return sync + COOP_SYNC_TARGET_STEP * number
end
-- Per-remote slots for more than two players (added by the SR2 co-op mod, appended to ug_lib.lua after coop_missions.lua).
-- A two-player script gives the remote side one HUD slot, one seat or one "other player"; these give every remote its own.

COOP_TRACE_PREFIX = "coop: "

-- Writes text to the adapter log when trace=1: mission_debug is a native that does nothing, the mod's LT1 hook reads it.
function coop_trace(text)
	mission_debug(COOP_TRACE_PREFIX .. text)
end

-- The number n of the script name "#PLAYERn#", or nil. The game hands the names out lowest number first, so with four
-- players the remotes are #PLAYER2# to #PLAYER4# (COOP_PLAYER_NUMBER, coop_outfit_sync.lua, lists the remote names).
function coop_player_number(name)
	if name == LOCAL_PLAYER then
		return 1
	end
	return COOP_PLAYER_NUMBER[name]
end

-- The HUD slot (bar, timer or objective index) of player name: local_slot for the local player, remote_slots[n - 1] for
-- "#PLAYERn#", and remote_slots[1], the remote side's slot of the two-player script, for a remote without an entry.
function coop_hud_slot(name, local_slot, remote_slots)
	if name == LOCAL_PLAYER then
		return local_slot
	end
	local n = coop_player_number(name)
	if n ~= nil and n >= 2 and remote_slots[n - 1] ~= nil then
		return remote_slots[n - 1]
	end
	return remote_slots[1]
end

-- A table of HUD slots keyed by player name, read like the two-player {[LOCAL_PLAYER] = a, [REMOTE_PLAYER] = b}.
function coop_hud_slots(local_slot, remote_slots)
	local slots = {}
	slots[LOCAL_PLAYER] = local_slot
	slots[REMOTE_PLAYER] = remote_slots[1]
	setmetatable(slots, {
		__index = function(table_, name)
			if not coop_is_remote_player(name) then
				return nil
			end
			local slot = coop_hud_slot(name, local_slot, remote_slots)
			rawset(table_, name, slot)
			coop_trace("hud slot " .. name .. " " .. slot)
			return slot
		end
	})
	return slots
end

-- fn(slot) once for every distinct slot the remote players have in slots (a coop_hud_slots table).
function coop_each_remote_slot(fn, slots)
	local done = {}
	for i, p in pairs(coop_remote_players()) do
		local slot = slots[p]
		if slot ~= nil and not done[slot] then
			done[slot] = true
			fn(slot)
		end
	end
end

-- The names of every player but name, the local player first.
function coop_other_players(name)
	local others = {}
	for i, p in ipairs(coop_all_players()) do
		if p ~= name then
			others[coop_count(others) + 1] = p
		end
	end
	return others
end

-- True when state[p] == value for any player p other than name.
function coop_any_other_equal(state, name, value)
	for i, p in ipairs(coop_other_players(name)) do
		if state[p] == value then
			return true
		end
	end
	return false
end

-- The remote players p with state[p] == value, in coop_remote_players() order.
function coop_remotes_equal(state, value)
	local found = {}
	for i, p in ipairs(coop_remote_players()) do
		if state[p] == value then
			found[coop_count(found) + 1] = p
		end
	end
	return found
end

-- True when fn(p, ...) is true for any player p other than excluded.
function coop_any_other(fn, excluded, ...)
	for i, p in ipairs(coop_other_players(excluded)) do
		if fn(p, unpack(arg, 1, arg.n)) then
			return true
		end
	end
	return false
end

-- True when state[name] >= value for every remote player.
function coop_all_remotes_at_least(state, value)
	for i, p in pairs(coop_remote_players()) do
		if state[p] < value then
			return false
		end
	end
	return true
end

-- The player after name in coop_all_players() order, from the last back to the first (two players: the other one).
function coop_next_player(name)
	local players = coop_all_players()
	local count = coop_count(players)
	for i = 1, count do
		if players[i] == name then
			if i == count then
				return players[1]
			end
			return players[i + 1]
		end
	end
	return players[1]
end

-- The first player after name, in coop_next_player order, for which fn(p) is true, or nil.
function coop_next_player_where(name, fn)
	local p = name
	for i = 2, coop_count(coop_all_players()) do
		p = coop_next_player(p)
		if fn(p) then
			return p
		end
	end
	return nil
end

-- The player other than excluded nearest to object, a living one first; with no other player alive, the nearest one.
function coop_nearest_other_player(object, excluded)
	local best = nil
	local best_dist = nil
	local best_living = false
	for i, p in ipairs(coop_other_players(excluded)) do
		local living = not COOP_NATIVE.character_is_dead(p)
		local dist = COOP_NATIVE.get_dist(p, object)
		if best == nil or (living and not best_living) or (living == best_living and dist < best_dist) then
			best = p
			best_dist = dist
			best_living = living
		end
	end
	return best
end

-- The player other than excluded with state[p] true that is nearest to object, else get_other_coop_player(excluded).
function coop_nearest_other_in(state, object, excluded)
	local best = nil
	local best_dist = nil
	for i, p in ipairs(coop_other_players(excluded)) do
		if state[p] then
			local dist = COOP_NATIVE.get_dist(p, object)
			if best == nil or dist < best_dist then
				best = p
				best_dist = dist
			end
		end
	end
	return best or get_other_coop_player(excluded)
end

-- The smallest distance from object of the players in the list players (COOP_FAR_DISTANCE for an empty list).
function coop_nearest_dist_of(players, object)
	local nearest = COOP_FAR_DISTANCE
	for i, p in ipairs(players) do
		local dist = COOP_NATIVE.get_dist(p, object)
		if dist < nearest then
			nearest = dist
		end
	end
	return nearest
end

-- The results of fn(...) for the remote player that makes result number rank_index the smallest (REMOTE_PLAYER among
-- the arguments stands for each remote in turn).
function coop_best_remote(fn, rank_index, ...)
	local at = coop_remote_arg_index(arg)
	local best = nil
	for i, p in pairs(coop_remote_players()) do
		local copy = coop_args_for(arg, at, p)
		local results = { fn(unpack(copy, 1, copy.n)) }
		if best == nil or results[rank_index] < best[rank_index] then
			best = results
		end
	end
	return unpack(best)
end

-- True when every player's vehicle in vehicles (a player table) is vehicles[name].
function coop_all_in_vehicle_of(vehicles, name)
	for i, p in ipairs(coop_other_players(name)) do
		if vehicles[p] ~= vehicles[name] then
			return false
		end
	end
	return true
end
-- Calls that name REMOTE_PLAYER (the one partner of the two-player scripts) act for every remote player.
-- A wrapper replaces the global function. It looks for REMOTE_PLAYER among the arguments and, when there is more than one
-- remote player, applies the function's rule; with one remote player (or none) it makes the original call unchanged.
--   fanout   the call is made once per remote player
--   seats    each remote player gets a seat of its own (coop_seats.lua)
--   seat_lock as fanout, except to a remote player that is on foot for lack of a seat (coop_seats.lua)
--   group    REMOTE_PLAYER in a list of characters is replaced by every remote player
--   target   the call is made for the remote player nearest to the first argument
--   all      true when the call is true for every remote player
--   any      true when the call is true for any remote player
--   nearest  the smallest value over the remote players

COOP_NATIVE = {}
COOP_ORIGINAL = {}
COOP_RULE = {}
-- Called with the arguments of a seat call that does not name REMOTE_PLAYER (coop_seats.lua fills it).
COOP_SEAT_CLAIM = {}

-- The function the game registered for a wrapper made by coop_wrap (any other function as it is).
function coop_native(fn)
	return COOP_ORIGINAL[fn] or fn
end

-- The position of the first REMOTE_PLAYER in the argument table, or nil.
function coop_remote_arg_index(args)
	for i = 1, args.n do
		if args[i] == REMOTE_PLAYER then
			return i
		end
	end
	return nil
end

-- A copy of the arguments with player at position at.
function coop_args_for(args, at, player)
	local copy = { n = args.n }
	for i = 1, args.n do
		copy[i] = args[i]
	end
	copy[at] = player
	return copy
end

function COOP_RULE.fanout(native, args, at, remotes)
	local first = nil
	for i, p in ipairs(remotes) do
		local copy = coop_args_for(args, at, p)
		local results = { native(unpack(copy, 1, copy.n)) }
		first = first or results
	end
	return unpack(first)
end

function COOP_RULE.all(native, args, at, remotes)
	for i, p in ipairs(remotes) do
		local copy = coop_args_for(args, at, p)
		if not native(unpack(copy, 1, copy.n)) then
			return false
		end
	end
	return true
end

function COOP_RULE.any(native, args, at, remotes)
	for i, p in ipairs(remotes) do
		local copy = coop_args_for(args, at, p)
		if native(unpack(copy, 1, copy.n)) then
			return true
		end
	end
	return false
end

function COOP_RULE.nearest(native, args, at, remotes)
	local nearest = nil
	for i, p in ipairs(remotes) do
		local copy = coop_args_for(args, at, p)
		local dist = native(unpack(copy, 1, copy.n))
		if nearest == nil or dist < nearest then
			nearest = dist
		end
	end
	return nearest
end

function COOP_RULE.target(native, args, at, remotes)
	local chosen = remotes[1]
	if at ~= 1 then
		local chosen_dist = nil
		for i, p in ipairs(remotes) do
			local dist = COOP_NATIVE.get_dist(args[1], p)
			if chosen_dist == nil or dist < chosen_dist then
				chosen = p
				chosen_dist = dist
			end
		end
	end
	local copy = coop_args_for(args, at, chosen)
	return native(unpack(copy, 1, copy.n))
end

function COOP_RULE.group(native, args, at, remotes)
	local copy = { n = 0 }
	for i = 1, args.n do
		if i == at then
			for k, p in ipairs(remotes) do
				copy.n = copy.n + 1
				copy[copy.n] = p
			end
		else
			copy.n = copy.n + 1
			copy[copy.n] = args[i]
		end
	end
	return native(unpack(copy, 1, copy.n))
end

-- Replaces the global function name with a wrapper that applies rule around native (default: the current function).
-- A name that is not defined, or is already wrapped, is left alone.
function coop_wrap(name, rule, native)
	if COOP_ORIGINAL[_G[name]] ~= nil then
		return
	end
	native = native or _G[name]
	if native == nil or COOP_RULE[rule] == nil then
		return
	end
	local handler = COOP_RULE[rule]
	local wrapper = function(...)
		local at = coop_remote_arg_index(arg)
		if at == nil then
			if COOP_SEAT_CLAIM[name] ~= nil then
				COOP_SEAT_CLAIM[name](name, arg)
			end
			return native(unpack(arg, 1, arg.n))
		end
		local remotes = coop_remote_players()
		if coop_count(remotes) < 2 or (rule == "group" and type(arg[1]) == "table") then
			return native(unpack(arg, 1, arg.n))
		end
		return handler(native, arg, at, remotes, name)
	end
	COOP_NATIVE[name] = native
	COOP_ORIGINAL[wrapper] = native
	_G[name] = wrapper
end
-- Vehicle seating for three or four players (added by the SR2 co-op mod, appended to ug_lib.lua after coop_wrappers.lua).
-- The scripts seat REMOTE_PLAYER, and the NPCs and the local player around it, at fixed seats. With more than one remote player
-- the k-th remote (k = 1 is REMOTE_PLAYER) gets a seat of its own: the scripted seat for REMOTE_PLAYER, else a free seat of the
-- vehicle, else a seat of another vehicle, else it stays on foot. A seat the script then gives to someone else is taken from the
-- extra remote. The in-vehicle query follows the placement, so a wait for "every remote in the vehicle" ends.
-- With fewer than two remotes, or when the game's query natives are missing, the k-th remote takes the seat k - 1 places after
-- the scripted one.

COOP_SEAT_ARG = { vehicle_enter_teleport = 3, vehicle_enter = 3, player_force_vehicle_seat = 2 }
COOP_SEAT_VEHICLE_ARG = { vehicle_enter_teleport = 2, vehicle_enter = 2, player_force_vehicle_seat = 3 }
COOP_SEAT_FORCE = "player_force_vehicle_seat"
COOP_SEAT_FIRST_PASSENGER = 1
COOP_SEAT_ON_FOOT = "on foot"

-- The natives of the game, taken before the wrappers replace them.
COOP_SEAT_RAW = {
	in_vehicle = character_is_in_vehicle,
	occupant = get_char_in_vehicle,
	num_seats = vehicle_get_num_seats,
	vehicle_name = get_char_vehicle_name,
	enter_done = vehicle_enter_check_done,
	debug = mission_debug,
}

COOP_SEAT_PLACED = {}  -- [remote][vehicle the script named] = { vehicle, seat, request, k } or COOP_SEAT_ON_FOOT
COOP_SEAT_LAST = {}    -- [remote] = the last placement of that remote
COOP_SEAT_CLAIMS = {}  -- [character] = { vehicle, seat } of its last enter call
COOP_SEAT_FORCED = {}  -- [player] = { vehicle, seat } of its forced seat
COOP_SEAT_ASKED = {}   -- [remote and vehicle] = the last answer of the in-vehicle query that was logged

-- True when the natives that tell who sits where exist (the unit test harness has none).
function coop_seat_ready()
	return COOP_SEAT_RAW.in_vehicle ~= nil and COOP_SEAT_RAW.occupant ~= nil and COOP_SEAT_RAW.num_seats ~= nil
		and COOP_SEAT_RAW.vehicle_name ~= nil and COOP_SEAT_RAW.enter_done ~= nil
end

-- The adapter logs the texts that start with "coop seat " (mission_debug does nothing else).
function coop_seat_trace(text)
	if COOP_SEAT_RAW.debug ~= nil then
		COOP_SEAT_RAW.debug("coop seat " .. text)
	end
end

function coop_seat_use(used, vehicle, seat)
	used[vehicle .. "/" .. seat] = true
end

-- The seats a remote after the first may take in a vehicle of n seats: the seats after the scripted one, then the ones before
-- it. The driver seat 0 and the scripted seat are never in the list.
function coop_seat_candidates(n, scripted)
	local list = {}
	local count = 0
	for seat = scripted + 1, n - 1 do
		count = count + 1
		list[count] = seat
	end
	for seat = COOP_SEAT_FIRST_PASSENGER, scripted - 1 do
		if seat < n then
			count = count + 1
			list[count] = seat
		end
	end
	return list
end

-- True when the character that claimed a seat is still in the vehicle or still on its way in.
function coop_seat_claim_live(char, claim)
	if COOP_SEAT_RAW.in_vehicle(char, claim.vehicle) then
		return true
	end
	local done = COOP_SEAT_RAW.enter_done(char)
	return done == false or done == 0
end

-- True when somebody sits in the seat, is entering it, has it forced, or was just given it (used).
-- The occupant lookup answers nil while a character is entering or leaving, so the claims cover that.
function coop_seat_taken(vehicle, seat, used)
	if COOP_SEAT_RAW.occupant(vehicle, seat) ~= nil or used[vehicle .. "/" .. seat] then
		return true
	end
	for char, claim in pairs(COOP_SEAT_CLAIMS) do
		if claim.vehicle == vehicle and claim.seat == seat then
			if coop_seat_claim_live(char, claim) then
				return true
			end
			COOP_SEAT_CLAIMS[char] = nil
		end
	end
	for player, forced in pairs(COOP_SEAT_FORCED) do
		if forced.vehicle == vehicle and forced.seat == seat then
			return true
		end
	end
	return false
end

-- The first free candidate seat of the vehicle, and its seat count (0 when the vehicle is not resolved yet).
function coop_seat_pick(vehicle, scripted, used)
	local n = COOP_SEAT_RAW.num_seats(vehicle)
	if type(n) ~= "number" or n <= 0 then
		return nil, 0
	end
	local candidates = coop_seat_candidates(n, scripted)
	for i = 1, coop_count(candidates) do
		if not coop_seat_taken(vehicle, candidates[i], used) then
			return candidates[i], n
		end
	end
	return nil, n
end

-- The vehicles a remote may be seated in instead of target: the local player's, then the other remotes', in list order.
function coop_seat_fallbacks(p, target)
	local list = {}
	local count = 0
	local function add(vehicle)
		if vehicle == nil or vehicle == target then
			return
		end
		for i = 1, count do
			if list[i] == vehicle then
				return
			end
		end
		count = count + 1
		list[count] = vehicle
	end
	add(COOP_SEAT_RAW.vehicle_name(LOCAL_PLAYER))
	for i, other in ipairs(coop_remote_players()) do
		if other ~= p then
			add(COOP_SEAT_RAW.vehicle_name(other))
		end
	end
	return list
end

-- The first fallback vehicle with a free passenger seat, and that seat; nil when there is none.
function coop_seat_fallback(p, target, used)
	local vehicles = coop_seat_fallbacks(p, target)
	for i = 1, coop_count(vehicles) do
		local n = COOP_SEAT_RAW.num_seats(vehicles[i])
		if type(n) == "number" then
			for seat = COOP_SEAT_FIRST_PASSENGER, n - 1 do
				if not coop_seat_taken(vehicles[i], seat, used) then
					return vehicles[i], seat
				end
			end
		end
	end
	return nil, nil
end

-- Enters remote p (the k-th) as the request says: the scripted vehicle and a free seat in it, else another vehicle, else not at all.
-- The request is { name, args, at } of the script's call. used lists the seats given out by the call in progress.
function coop_seat_put(p, k, request, used)
	local seat_at = COOP_SEAT_ARG[request.name]
	local vehicle_at = COOP_SEAT_VEHICLE_ARG[request.name]
	local native = COOP_NATIVE[request.name]
	local vehicle = request.args[vehicle_at]
	local scripted = request.args[seat_at]
	local copy = coop_args_for(request.args, request.at, p)
	local placed = COOP_SEAT_PLACED[p]
	if placed == nil then
		placed = {}
		COOP_SEAT_PLACED[p] = placed
	end
	COOP_SEAT_CLAIMS[p] = nil
	local seat, n = coop_seat_pick(vehicle, scripted, used)
	local label = p .. " " .. vehicle .. " n=" .. n .. " seat " .. scripted .. " -> "
	if n == 0 then
		copy[seat_at] = scripted + k - 1
		native(unpack(copy, 1, copy.n))
		coop_seat_trace(label .. vehicle .. " " .. copy[seat_at] .. " (legacy)")
		return
	end
	local target = vehicle
	local how = "free"
	if seat == nil then
		target, seat = coop_seat_fallback(p, vehicle, used)
		how = "moved"
	end
	if seat == nil then
		placed[vehicle] = COOP_SEAT_ON_FOOT
		COOP_SEAT_LAST[p] = COOP_SEAT_ON_FOOT
		coop_seat_trace(label .. "none (on foot)")
		return
	end
	copy[vehicle_at] = target
	copy[seat_at] = seat
	native(unpack(copy, 1, copy.n))
	local placement = { vehicle = target, seat = seat, request = request, k = k }
	placed[vehicle] = placement
	COOP_SEAT_LAST[p] = placement
	COOP_SEAT_CLAIMS[p] = { vehicle = target, seat = seat }
	coop_seat_use(used, target, seat)
	coop_seat_trace(label .. target .. " " .. seat .. " (" .. how .. ")")
end

-- Takes the extra remotes out of a seat that a character is about to enter, and seats them again somewhere else.
function coop_seat_evict(vehicle, seat, char)
	local victims = {}
	local count = 0
	for k, p in ipairs(coop_remote_players()) do
		if k >= 2 and p ~= char and COOP_SEAT_PLACED[p] ~= nil then
			for intended, placement in pairs(COOP_SEAT_PLACED[p]) do
				if placement ~= COOP_SEAT_ON_FOOT and placement.vehicle == vehicle and placement.seat == seat then
					count = count + 1
					victims[count] = { player = p, k = k, intended = intended, request = placement.request }
				end
			end
		end
	end
	local used = {}
	coop_seat_use(used, vehicle, seat)
	for i = 1, count do
		local victim = victims[i]
		coop_seat_trace("evict " .. victim.player .. " from " .. vehicle .. " " .. seat .. " for " .. tostring(char))
		COOP_SEAT_PLACED[victim.player][victim.intended] = nil
		COOP_SEAT_CLAIMS[victim.player] = nil
		coop_native(vehicle_exit_teleport)(victim.player)
		coop_seat_put(victim.player, victim.k, victim.request, used)
	end
end

-- Called before every seat call that does not name REMOTE_PLAYER (and before the call for REMOTE_PLAYER itself): records the seat
-- as taken and gives it up from any extra remote that was placed in it.
function coop_seat_claim(name, args)
	if not coop_seat_ready() or coop_count(coop_remote_players()) < 2 then
		return
	end
	local char = args[1]
	local seat = args[COOP_SEAT_ARG[name]]
	local vehicle = args[COOP_SEAT_VEHICLE_ARG[name]]
	if name == COOP_SEAT_FORCE then
		COOP_SEAT_FORCED[char] = nil
		if type(seat) == "number" and seat >= 0 and vehicle ~= nil then
			COOP_SEAT_FORCED[char] = { vehicle = vehicle, seat = seat }
		end
		return
	end
	if vehicle == nil or type(seat) ~= "number" or seat < 0 then
		return
	end
	COOP_SEAT_CLAIMS[char] = { vehicle = vehicle, seat = seat }
	coop_seat_evict(vehicle, seat, char)
end

-- A forced seat of an extra remote: a free candidate seat of the vehicle; none, or no vehicle, forces nothing (-1: any free seat).
function coop_seat_force(native, p, k, copy, used)
	local seat = copy[2]
	local vehicle = copy[3]
	COOP_SEAT_FORCED[p] = nil
	if type(seat) ~= "number" or seat < 0 then
		native(unpack(copy, 1, copy.n))
		return
	end
	local chosen = nil
	local n = 0
	if vehicle ~= nil then
		chosen, n = coop_seat_pick(vehicle, seat, used)
	end
	local label = p .. " " .. tostring(vehicle) .. " " .. seat .. " -> "
	if vehicle ~= nil and n == 0 then
		copy[2] = seat + k - 1
		COOP_SEAT_FORCED[p] = { vehicle = vehicle, seat = copy[2] }
		native(unpack(copy, 1, copy.n))
		coop_seat_trace("force " .. label .. copy[2])
	elseif chosen == nil then
		native(p, -1)
		coop_seat_trace("force " .. label .. "-1")
	else
		copy[2] = chosen
		COOP_SEAT_FORCED[p] = { vehicle = vehicle, seat = chosen }
		coop_seat_use(used, vehicle, chosen)
		native(unpack(copy, 1, copy.n))
		coop_seat_trace("force " .. label .. chosen)
	end
end

-- The rule of the seat calls: the k-th remote after the first gets a seat of its own; a seat below 0 (a release) or none is not moved.
function coop_seat_place(native, args, at, remotes, name)
	local seat_at = COOP_SEAT_ARG[name]
	local vehicle_at = COOP_SEAT_VEHICLE_ARG[name]
	local ready = coop_seat_ready()
	local request = { name = name, args = args, at = at }
	local used = {}
	local first = nil
	for k, p in ipairs(remotes) do
		local copy = coop_args_for(args, at, p)
		local seat = args[seat_at]
		local results = nil
		if not ready then
			if type(seat) == "number" and seat >= 0 then
				copy[seat_at] = seat + k - 1
			end
			results = { native(unpack(copy, 1, copy.n)) }
		elseif k == 1 then
			coop_seat_claim(name, copy)
			if name ~= COOP_SEAT_FORCE and type(seat) == "number" and seat >= 0 and args[vehicle_at] ~= nil then
				coop_seat_use(used, args[vehicle_at], seat)
			end
			results = { native(unpack(copy, 1, copy.n)) }
		elseif name == COOP_SEAT_FORCE then
			coop_seat_force(native, p, k, copy, used)
		elseif type(seat) == "number" and seat >= 0 and args[vehicle_at] ~= nil then
			coop_seat_put(p, k, request, used)
		else
			native(unpack(copy, 1, copy.n))
		end
		first = first or results
	end
	return unpack(first)
end

-- The calls that stop remotes from entering vehicles skip the extra remotes that are on foot for lack of a seat: they keep their
-- chance to take a vehicle of their own.
function COOP_RULE.seat_lock(native, args, at, remotes)
	local first = nil
	for k, p in ipairs(remotes) do
		if args[2] == false and COOP_SEAT_LAST[p] == COOP_SEAT_ON_FOOT then
			coop_seat_trace("keep entry " .. p .. " (on foot)")
		else
			local copy = coop_args_for(args, at, p)
			local results = { native(unpack(copy, 1, copy.n)) }
			first = first or results
		end
	end
	return unpack(first or {})
end

-- character_is_in_vehicle for a remote that was given a seat of another vehicle asks about that vehicle; one that stayed on foot
-- answers as REMOTE_PLAYER does, which changes neither an "all" nor an "any" over the remotes.
function coop_seat_in_vehicle(...)
	local p = arg[1]
	local vehicle = arg[2]
	local placed = COOP_SEAT_PLACED[p]
	local placement = nil
	if placed ~= nil and vehicle ~= nil then
		placement = placed[vehicle]
	end
	if placement == nil then
		return COOP_SEAT_RAW.in_vehicle(unpack(arg, 1, arg.n))
	end
	local where = "mirror"
	local answer = nil
	if placement == COOP_SEAT_ON_FOOT then
		answer = COOP_SEAT_RAW.in_vehicle(REMOTE_PLAYER, vehicle)
	else
		where = placement.vehicle
		answer = COOP_SEAT_RAW.in_vehicle(p, where)
	end
	local key = p .. " " .. vehicle
	if COOP_SEAT_ASKED[key] ~= tostring(answer) then
		COOP_SEAT_ASKED[key] = tostring(answer)
		coop_seat_trace("ask " .. p .. " in " .. vehicle .. " -> " .. where .. " (" .. tostring(answer) .. ")")
	end
	return answer
end

-- The seat player was given in vehicle (the vehicle the script names), for the waits that follow a seat call: first_seat for the first
-- remote, whose seat is the script's, the seat of its placement, nil for a remote that stayed on foot or went to another vehicle.
function coop_seat_of(vehicle, player, first_seat)
	local placed = COOP_SEAT_PLACED[player]
	local placement = nil
	if placed ~= nil then
		placement = placed[vehicle]
	end
	if placement == nil then
		if player == coop_remote_players()[1] then
			return first_seat
		end
		return nil
	end
	if placement == COOP_SEAT_ON_FOOT or placement.vehicle ~= vehicle then
		return nil
	end
	return placement.seat
end

-- True when fn(p, vehicle) is true for every remote player that has a seat in vehicle.
function coop_all_seated(fn, vehicle)
	for i, p in ipairs(coop_remote_players()) do
		if coop_seat_of(vehicle, p, 0) ~= nil and not fn(p, vehicle) then
			return false
		end
	end
	return true
end

COOP_RULE.seats = coop_seat_place
COOP_SEAT_CLAIM.vehicle_enter_teleport = coop_seat_claim
COOP_SEAT_CLAIM.vehicle_enter = coop_seat_claim
COOP_SEAT_CLAIM.player_force_vehicle_seat = coop_seat_claim
-- Which rule (see coop_wrappers.lua) each function follows when it is called with REMOTE_PLAYER.

		"inv_item_add", "vehicle_exit_teleport", "vehicle_exit_dive", "character_release_human_shield", "thread_new",

	},

-- ug_lib functions that only call get_dist: wrapped around get_dist itself, so a call for one remote player is not
-- widened again by the get_dist wrapper.
COOP_DIST_ALIASES = { "get_dist_char_to_nav", "get_dist_char_to_char", "get_dist_char_to_vehicle" }

for rule, names in pairs(COOP_RULES) do
	for i, name in ipairs(names) do
		coop_wrap(name, rule)
	end
end

for i, name in ipairs(COOP_DIST_ALIASES) do
	coop_wrap(name, "nearest", COOP_NATIVE.get_dist)
end

-- The query follows the seat each remote player was given (coop_seats.lua).
coop_wrap("character_is_in_vehicle", "all", coop_seat_in_vehicle)
-- A waypoint a script sets for one remote player reaches that player's machine alone (adapter: waypoint_scope.cpp). The script names
-- the player through mission_debug, which does nothing else in the game, and the adapter sends the waypoints that follow to that
-- player until the name is cleared. Without the adapter's hooks the control text is a debug line and the waypoint reaches every remote.

COOP_SEND_TO = "coop_send_to"

-- True when waypoints for player must be named to the adapter: there is more than one remote player and player is one of them.
function coop_sends_to_one(player)
	return coop_count(coop_remote_players()) > 1 and coop_is_remote_player(player)
end

-- Sent to one remote, ug_lib's mission_waypoint_add and mission_waypoint_remove are made with the natives they call. Those two
-- keep one record for every machine (Mission_waypoint): a remove for one remote cleared it, so the next remote's remove was
-- skipped and that player kept the GPS. Here the remove always reaches the player and leaves the record, and the add sets it,
-- so a later mission-wide remove still runs. A remove when none is set does nothing in the game.
function coop_mission_waypoint_add_one(navpoint, sync)
	waypoint_remove(sync)
	Mission_waypoint = waypoint_add(navpoint, sync)
end

function coop_mission_waypoint_remove_one(sync)
	waypoint_remove(sync)
end

-- The function a call for one remote makes in place of the waypoint function the script named.
function coop_waypoint_one(waypoint_function)
	if waypoint_function == mission_waypoint_add then
		return coop_mission_waypoint_add_one
	elseif waypoint_function == mission_waypoint_remove then
		return coop_mission_waypoint_remove_one
	end
	return waypoint_function
end

-- Runs make() with the waypoint calls it makes named to player, then clears the name. The name is cleared also when make() raises an
-- error (the error is raised again), so the calls of every later script do not all go to that one player.
function coop_send_to_player(player, make)
	mission_debug(COOP_SEND_TO .. " " .. player)
	local ok, result = pcall(make)
	mission_debug(COOP_SEND_TO)
	if not ok then
		error(result)
	end
	return result
end

-- add(navpoint, sync) for player: sent to that player's machine alone when there is more than one remote player.
function coop_waypoint_add_for(player, add, navpoint, sync)
	if not coop_sends_to_one(player) then
		return add(navpoint, sync)
	end
	coop_trace("waypoint add " .. player)
	return coop_send_to_player(player, function() return coop_waypoint_one(add)(navpoint, sync) end)
end

-- remove(sync) for player: sent to that player's machine alone when there is more than one remote player.
function coop_waypoint_remove_for(player, remove, sync)
	if not coop_sends_to_one(player) then
		return remove(sync)
	end
	coop_trace("waypoint remove " .. player)
	return coop_send_to_player(player, function() return coop_waypoint_one(remove)(sync) end)
end

-- The name of the navpoint in navpoint_names closest to player, measured with the game's own get_dist so that a remote player is not
-- widened to the nearest remote.
function coop_closest_navpoint(navpoint_names, player)
	local measure = coop_native(get_dist)
	local closest_name = navpoint_names[1]
	local closest_dist = measure(player, navpoint_names[1])
	for index, name in pairs(navpoint_names) do
		local current = measure(player, name)
		if current < closest_dist then
			closest_name = name
			closest_dist = current
		end
	end
	return closest_name
end
